svg.title: When a lifecycle action really happens
svg.desc: An object created on 2 November 2026 at 14:20 UTC under a rule with Days 30 becomes eligible at the creation time plus 30 days rounded up to the next midnight UTC, 3 December 2026 00:00 UTC. Billing changes at that moment, except for transitions to Intelligent-Tiering, which are billed at the new rate only after the move. S3 evaluates rules once a day and queues the action, which runs asynchronously, often a day or more later. For tag-based rules the tags are checked again when the action runs. When it is done, a Lifecycle event notification, a CloudTrail lifecycle data event and a server access log record can confirm it. Rule changes take up to 15 minutes to propagate.
svg.text: When a lifecycle action really happens
Rule: Transitions Days 30 → STANDARD_IA, object created 2026-11-02 14:20 UTC
often a day or more later
STANDARD_IA rate from eligibility, even while the transition is still queued
Exception: a transition to INTELLIGENT_TIERING is billed at the new rate only after the object has moved.
Glacier classes: the new rate, the 40 KB overhead and the minimum-duration clock all start at eligibility. Expired objects: no storage billed after it.
head-object shows the expiry of the current version (Expiration field); nothing shows a planned transition.
A changed rule takes up to 15 minutes to propagate. A new rule applies to existing objects at the next evaluation.
Not a hard deadline: confirm deletions that must happen by a date with notifications, CloudTrail or S3 Inventory.
